summary: Role inheritance calculation bug prevents cross-project console elevation
description:
Issue summary:
Users who should receive temporary elevation via role inheritance (team -> project -> console-role) are not getting elevated roles after the scheduled Okta sync. This affects engineers attempting cross-project admin tasks using the Console elevation flow.

Impact:
- Multiple engineers reported Access Denied when attempting to open elevated admin pages across projects (error 403 with RBAC check failed).
- Blocking cross-project triage and incident response for several P0/P1 incidents this week.
- Affects approx. 12 users in the SRE and Platform teams; broader groups may be impacted but not yet reported.

Observed behavior:
- Okta group sync completes without errors per provisioner logs.
- Console authorization layer denies access due to missing "inherited_roles" entries in the internal RBAC cache for affected users.
- Manual role recompute (admin console -> Recalculate Roles) restores access for a user temporarily.

Expected behavior:
- After Okta sync completes, role inheritance should be recomputed or queued so users immediately gain derived roles (project-level roles and console elevation permissions) without manual intervention.

Context and recent changes:
- Rolled out RBAC service refactor on 2026-03-08 to optimize inheritance calculation for large orgs (PR: github.com/redwood/infra/commit/3a9f2b8).
- Okta provisioner upgrade (2026-03-09) changed the group-change webhook payload shape to include `changed_members` as an array of objects. RBAC recompute job expects `changed_members` as a flat list of strings. This mismatch likely skipped enqueueing recompute jobs for some user events.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Identify an engineer with team-level group membership that should inherit project-admin role via policy.
2) Trigger a synthetic Okta group-change event for that user (okta-provisioner/simulate-membership-change).
3) Observe provisioner logs: webhook accepted and processed (no errors), but the RBAC recompute queue does not receive a message for that user.
4) Attempt to perform a cross-project admin action in Console -> Access Control and observe 403 with 'rbac.authorization.inherited_missing' message in response header.
logs: 2026-03-11T09:12:03Z okta-provisioner INFO received webhook id=wh_1a2b payload_size=4
2026-03-11T09:12:04Z rbac-service WARN recompute-handler skipped 0 events (payload shape mismatch)
investigation_notes: 03/11 11:00 - Support triaged: replicated with synthetic webhook; observed mismatch between provisioner payload and recompute handler schema.
03/11 13:30 - Reproducer: manually POSTed older payload shape -> recompute job enqueued and user gained inherited roles immediately.
03/12 08:45 - Reviewed PR 3a9f2b8 (rbac refactor): code assumes changed_members is list<string>. New provisioner sends list<object>.
03/12 10:10 - Hypothesis: type check in rbac-service swallowed the event without logging full payload for privacy; added debug hook to log sanitized payloads.
03/13 16:00 - Confirmed: handler returns early on payload element type mismatch. Fix is to accept object form and extract .id field, fallback to string when present.
comments: Maya Patel (Support) 2026-03-10: Initial report from SRE oncall: 'can't escalate to project admin after policy change'. Filed ticket and added Lina.
Lina Becker (Identity) 2026-03-11: Reproduced locally using synthetic webhook. Attaching logs. Suspect schema mismatch introduced by okta-provisioner 2026-03-09 deploy.
Ethan Morales (SRE) 2026-03-11: Workaround: run 'rbacctl recompute --user U123' which granted the inherited role. Need an automated fix for bulk affected users.
Lina Becker 2026-03-12: Drafted small patch to rbac-service that normalizes changed_members entries. Running unit tests; will deploy canary to staging today.
Alex Chen (Oncall) 2026-03-13: Confirmed patch on staging; recompute queue now receives events. Requested deployment to prod with 10m canary before full rollout.
Maya Patel 2026-03-14: Notified affected teams and opened a short incident postmortem page. Collecting list of users impacted for retroactive recompute.
workaround: Manual recompute using 'rbacctl recompute --user <user-id>' or triggering admin console 'Recalculate Roles' on affected user. For bulk, run rbacctl --input users.csv --batch-recompute.
next_steps: 1) Merge and deploy rbac-service patch that accepts the object-shaped changed_members and extracts .id (PR: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4821).
2) Deploy to prod behind a 10-minute canary in us-east, monitor recompute-queue metrics and console authorization 403 rates.
3) Run bulk recompute job for window 2026-03-08..2026-03-12 for users who had Okta group changes (job id: recompute-bulk-20260314).
4) Postmortem: write RCA, timeline, and add a contract test between okta-provisioner and rbac-service to prevent payload-breakage.
5) Consider adding a safeguard: if recompute-handler sees unknown payload shape, it should still enqueue a fallback job for affected user IDs when possible.
